title: Execution-path selection regression: stabilize runtime dispatch and capacity-fencing playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: During a weekend capacity surge on 2026-02-09 we observed a sustained regression in request tail latency (p95/p99) for several hosted model routes. Impacted routes used the execution dispatch that selects optimized kernels and attention tiling heuristics. The regression manifested as intermittent 2-5x increases in p95 for text-generation workloads and a measurable drop in throughput under burst traffic. This ticket captures the follow-ups, a stabilization playbook, and concrete action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-09 02:10 UTC - Alert: routing-based p95 spikes on prod-hosted; 2026-02-09 02:25 UTC - Canary rollback to runtime-1.25 reduced spikes; 2026-02-09 03:00 UTC - Root-cause triage began; 2026-02-09 09:30 UTC - Hotfix: pinned dispatch policy to conservative path; 2026-02-11 11:00 UTC - First mitigation PR opened; 2026-02-12 16:20 UTC - Telemetry added for kernel-selection decisions; 2026-02-15 10:40 UTC - Quarantine probe feature merged; 2026-02-18 14:10 UTC - Stabilization PR under review.
impact_details: Symptoms: increased p95/p99 latency for generation endpoints, reduced overall throughput on affected GPU pools, autoscaler oscillation leading to capacity thrash. Customer impact: a subset of customers saw increased response times and a small number of timed-out requests during peak bursts (estimated <0.5% of requests but higher for routes pinned to the affected path). Internal impact: SLO burn and on-call load for infra teams.
root_cause_summary: Primary cause: a recent change in the execution-path dispatch heuristic (merged as PR #5482) increased the aggressiveness of speculative kernel selection for long-sequence attention tiling. Under real-world sequence-length distributions this led to increased KV-cache fragmentation and higher probe costs, which interacted poorly with the scheduler's batch-filling logic and caused head-of-line blocking. Secondary factors: autoscaler hysteresis and insufficient telemetry on dispatch outcomes meant the issue amplified before detection.
mitigation_performed: Immediate: rolled back the speculative dispatch change on critical pools; applied a conservative dispatch pin for high-latency-sensitive routes; temporarily increased warm pool capacity to absorb traffic while fixes were validated. Medium-term: added finer-grained dispatch telemetry and a quarantine mechanism for experimental kernel probes.
action_items:
1) Add deterministic unit and integration tests that simulate mixed sequence-length distributions against dispatch heuristics (owner: Priya Desai, estimate: 3).
2) Implement a soft-fallback policy: measure probe cost in-situ and automatically prefer conservative kernels when probe penalty > X ms for 95th percentile (owner: Rafael Kim, estimate: 5).
3) Capacity-fence: allow autoscaler to respect a minimum steady-state reserve for routes tagged latency-critical (owner: Diego Alvarez, estimate: 3).
4) Telemetry: expand dispatch decision logs and surface reasons in the Console per-route diagnostics (owner: Mina Chen, estimate: 3).
5) Release gating: add a runtime canary rule that requires no p95 regressions over 4 hours on synthetic mixed-length traffic before wide deployment (owner: SRE team, estimate: 2).
6) Playbook: publish an incident playbook for dispatch regressions with step-by-step mitigations and rollback commands (owner: Ava Martinez, estimate: 2).
7) Post-deploy verification: add automated smoke tests that run scheduled probes against production pools after every runtime rollout (owner: QA, estimate: 2).
owners_and_estimates: Priya Desai - tests (3), Rafael Kim - soft-fallback policy (5), Diego Alvarez - autoscaler fencing (3), Mina Chen - telemetry & Console surfaces (3), SRE - canary gating (2), QA - post-deploy smoke (2).
acceptance_criteria: 1) No p95 regressions attributable to dispatch decisions in the next two full canary cycles (measured on synthetic and live mixed-length traffic). 2) Autopsy telemetry shows >=90% of dispatch decisions have a logged rationale and probe latency. 3) Autoscaler fencing prevents capacity thrash during representative bursts in load tests. 4) Playbook published and reviewed by SRE and runtime owners.

postmortem_conclusion: This regression surface is caused by an overly-aggressive optimization path that lacked sufficient real-world validation. With the combination of conservative default behavior, richer telemetry, gating in CI/canary, and autoscaler fences we expect to reduce the probability and impact of similar incidents. The planned actions prioritize observability and safe defaults over speculative performance wins.
next_steps: Finish stabilization PR reviews, run two full canary cycles with synthetic mixed-length workload, publish the playbook, and schedule a post-implementation review two weeks after full rollout.
